title: Hang a server's tool-less sliding rail in a 4-post rack: back end into the marked U, then draw out the front and seat it
instruction: Hang the rail on the marked U, back end first, then the front, then let go.
context: Racking servers is core data-centre work. Dell's installation sheet for its tool-less ReadyRails II sliding rails gives the steps: "Align each end piece in the bottom and top holes of the desired U spaces. Engage the back end of the rail until it fully seats on the vertical rack flange and the latch clicks into place. Repeat these steps to position and seat the front end piece on the vertical rack flange." The rail here is that kit's B6 rail, the 1U rail of the PowerEdge R640. The rack's flanges are a typical 0.74 m apart, longer than the collapsed rail. In the demo both hands carry the rail in level and push its back end home; then one hand lets go and the other draws the front member out along its slide to the front flange, matches it to the same U and pushes it home.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A 4-post open-frame rack of black powder-coated steel (shown 29 cm tall, six U of holes) with square-hole flanges (EIA-310: 9.5 mm square holes, three to each 44.45 mm U) stands on the table: its near pair of posts at x 28, the rear flange's inner face at y 37 and the front flange's at y -37 (0.74 m apart); the far pair of posts at x 76. Both near flanges have their third U from the bottom marked with yellow lines (its holes 10.1, 11.7 and 13.3 cm up). A Dell B6 ReadyRails II sliding rail, the tool-less 1U rail of the PowerEdge R640, lies on the table at (18, 0), along y, its back end toward +y. It is zinc-plated steel: an outer member carrying the back end piece, and a front member carrying the front end piece, which slides out along it to set the rail's length between flanges over Dell's square-hole range, 630 to 883 mm (it starts collapsed, 0.63 m). Each end piece carries two square pegs, at the bottom and top holes of a U, and a spring latch with its release button at the end piece's midpoint. Simulation settings, as Dell publishes none: an 18 x 40 mm channel; 1.35 kg; pegs tapered from 7.5 to 4.5 mm over 9 mm; a 3 N drag on the slide; a 10 N detent over the latch's last 3 mm. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Checked by looking at the rail's pegs in the flanges' holes and with a spirit level, as a technician checks. 1.0: both end pieces latched at the marked U (each pushed home on its flange with its two pegs in that U's bottom and top holes), the rail level within 0.5 degrees (its length's angle from horizontal), and every fingertip 3 cm or more from the rail's line (the line through its middle along its length), held 2 s. 0.25: the back end latched at the marked U, without the 1.0 result (this includes a front end latched a U off, a sloping rail). 0 otherwise (a rail hung reversed, its back end at the front flange, scores 0), or if the rail falls after an end piece has latched.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The rail's length range is Dell's (630 to 883 mm); its mass, section, peg taper, slide drag and latch detent are simulation settings, not measurements. The latch is coded: an end piece with both pegs within 1 mm of one U's holes must pass the detent over its last 3 mm, then is held where it seated. The rail's inner server slide is not modelled; it stays shut while the rail is hung. The far posts are drawn only.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Press each end piece's latch release and lift its pegs out of the flange, slide the front member back until the rail is collapsed, and lay the rail on the table at (18, 0) along y, its back end toward +y, as at the start.
